Group: TRANSACTION CORE — identity and direction of every transaction

Enum Values / Format: TXN-YYYYMMDD-XXXXX
Justification: Auto-generated unique identifier for every transaction record. Format encodes date + sequence. Dedup key used for cross-referencing with contracts, contacts, and payment gateway records. Never manually edited after creation.

Enum Values / Format: Credit / Debit
Justification: Direction of money flow from the platform's perspective. Credit = money coming in (e.g. tenant paying rent). Debit = money going out (e.g. landlord payout, refund). Always set explicitly — never inferred — to prevent reconciliation errors.

Enum Values / Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Justification: Date the transaction actually occurred — not the date the record was created. Used for period-level financial reporting and reconciliation. May differ from created_date if entered retrospectively or imported from a payment gateway.

Enum Values / Format: Positive value only
Justification: Transaction value in INR. Always stored as a positive number regardless of Credit/Debit direction. Direction is captured separately in credit_debit. Enables clean aggregations without sign-handling logic.

Enum Values / Format: Pending / Completed / Failed / Reversed / Disputed / Approved
Justification: Current state of the transaction. Pending = initiated but not confirmed. Completed = money moved and confirmed. Failed = attempt rejected by gateway. Reversed = completed but subsequently reversed (e.g. chargeback, reversal). Disputed = under investigation. Drives collection workflows and reconciliation flags.

Group: TRANSACTION CLASSIFICATION — what this transaction is for

Enum Values / Format: OPEX, CAPEX, INTEREST, SALARY, REIMBURSEMENT, REVENUE, REFUNDS, COGS
Justification: Top-level accounting classification. Maps directly to P&L and balance sheet line items. Revenue = income from tenants. COGS = direct cost of delivering the service (e.g. landlord payout). OpEx = operating expenses. Transfer = inter-account movement. Drives financial reporting rollups and period-close.

Enum Values / Format: DEPOSIT, TRANSPORT, FIXTURES, OFFICE, EMPLOYEE, CONSULTANT, CONTRACTOR, INVENTORY, TECH, MARKETING, FOOD AND BEVERAGES,
Justification: Sub-classification within Category 1. Maps the transaction to the specific business event it represents. Essential for contract-level P&L reconciliation — e.g. distinguishing Rent from FMR from SD even when all are Revenue. This is the field that links financial data back to the tenant lifecycle stages.

Enum Values / Format: Standard / Advance / Reversal / Refund / Write-off / Depreciation / SDT (Security Deposit Tenant) / SDM (Security Deposit Merchant) / Advance / Adjustment / Write-off
Justification: Accounting-level detail beneath Category 2. Used for specific transaction subtypes that require different treatment. SDT = deposit received from the tenants. SDM = deposit from merchants. Depreciation = asset write-down entry. Adjustment = correction to a prior transaction. Essential for accurate books.

Group: TRANSACTION PARTIES — who money flows between

Enum Values / Format: Company name or individual full name
Justification: Name of the entity sending money. Free text (not a lookup) to handle external parties not in CRM — e.g. tenants paying via bank transfer with no HubSpot record, or third-party employers. For internal parties, use exact registered name for reconciliation consistency.

Enum Values / Format: Tenant / Landlord / Vendor / Platform / Third Party / Government
Justification: Classification of the payer. Enables filtering without text matching on from_party names. Tenant = rent payments, deposits. Landlord = rare (e.g. landlord contributing to repairs). Platform = internal transfer. Government = TDS refunds, GST credits.

Enum Values / Format: GST Number, PAN Card, Address etc
Justification: GSTIN number, Address of the person paying the money

Enum Values / Format: Company name or individual full name
Justification: Name of the entity receiving money. Free text for same reasons as from_party. For tenant-facing transactions: platform receives. For landlord payouts: landlord name. For refunds: tenant name.

Enum Values / Format: Tenant / Landlord / Vendor / Platform / Third Party / Government
Justification: Classification of the payee. Mirrors from_party_type logic. Together from_party_type + to_party_type defines the transaction's commercial path (e.g. Tenant → Platform for rent collection, Platform → Landlord for payouts).

Enum Values / Format: GST Number, PAN Card, Address etc
Justification: GSTIN number, Address etc

Group: PAYMENT DETAILS — how and where money moved

Enum Values / Format: UPI / NEFT / RTGS / IMPS / Auto-debit (NACH) / Virtual Account / Payment Link / Cheque / Cash / Other
Justification: How the payment was made. Changed from free text to enum — free text creates inconsistent values ("upi", "UPI", "Upi") that break aggregation. Enum enforces consistency. Drives collection method analysis: which mediums have highest success rates, fastest settlement, lowest failure rates.

Enum Values / Format: Kotak / IDFC / Razorpayx / Volopay
Justification: Through which bank or medium the payment was made

Enum Values / Format: e.g. pay_xxxxxxxx (Razorpay) or order_xxxxxxxx (Cashfree)
Justification: Reference ID from the payment gateway (Razorpay, Cashfree etc.). Primary key for reconciliation between HubSpot transaction records and gateway dashboards. Enables looking up the exact payment in the gateway portal for dispute resolution.

Enum Values / Format: UTR / Settlement batch ID
Justification: Bank settlement reference or UTR number. Distinct from gateway reference — this is the interbank identifier after the gateway settles funds to the platform account. Used for bank statement reconciliation.

Group: TRANSACTION AUDIT — who created, approved, and when

Enum Values / Format: Full name or user ID
Justification: Who created this transaction record. System auto-captures the logged-in HubSpot user if using HubSpot native record creation. Manual fallback for records created via API or import. Audit trail — cannot be edited after creation.

Timestamp when the record was created in the system. Distinct from transaction_date (when the money moved). Auto-set by system. Used to detect backdated entries: large gap between created_date and transaction_date warrants review.

Enum Values / Format: Full name or user ID
Justification: Who approved this transaction. Separate from created_by to enforce dual-control — the same person should not create and authorise a transaction. Critical for financial compliance and fraud prevention. Required field for all Debit transactions above a threshold.

Timestamp when the record was approved in the system. Distinct from transaction_date (when the money moved). Auto-set by system. Used to detect backdated entries: large gap between created_date and transaction_date warrants review.

Free text notes for ops or finance team. Not visible to tenants or landlords. Used for exceptions, manual adjustments, and audit context (e.g. "late entry — payment confirmed via WhatsApp screenshot on date X"). Append-only in practice to preserve history.

Group: LINE ITEMS — breakdown of what this transaction covers

⚠ ARCHITECTURE NOTE: If a single transaction can have more than one line item (e.g. rent + maintenance + utility in one payment), line items should be a separate associated object — not fields on this record. The fields below are correct if each transaction maps to exactly one line item. Flag this before build.

Enum Values / Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Justification: Date specific to this line item. May differ from transaction_date — e.g. a payment made on the 5th may cover rent for the 1st. Used for period-accurate accrual accounting and month-close allocation.

Enum Values / Format: eg: Property Onboarding & Set up / Tech & Platform / Payment Processing / Operations / Furniture & Inventory
Justification: Internal accounting code attributing this line item to a specific property, city, or business unit. Enables P&L at the property level (PID), city level, or product line level. Should be standardised — consider making this an enum once cost centers are defined.

Human-readable explanation of what this line item covers, beyond what the category fields capture. E.g. "August rent for Room 3B, pro-rated for 25 days". The narrative layer for audit and dispute resolution.

Enum Values / Format: File URL (comma-separated if multiple) or attachment
Justification: Supporting documents for this line item: invoices, receipts, payment confirmation screenshots, bank statements. Stored as file URLs. Essential for audit trail and dispute resolution. Multiple files comma-separated or stored as a multi-file field depending on HubSpot configuration.

Group: TRANSACTION LINKS — associations to other objects ★ Recommended additions not in original spec

Enum Values / Format: {Party}_{PID}_{RID}_{Start Date}
Justification: ★ RECOMMENDED. Links this transaction to a specific Contract. Without this, you cannot do contract-level P&L (e.g. total revenue collected vs total costs for contract X). This is the single most important link — every financial transaction should be traceable to a contract.

Enum Values / Format: Merchant ID / Tenant ID / Vendor ID
Justification: ★ RECOMMENDED. Links this transaction to the tenant Contact record. Enables tenant-level financial history: all payments a tenant has made across all tenures. Required for FNF calculation and win-back analysis.
★ RECOMMENDED. Property ID this transaction relates to. Enables property-level revenue and cost reporting without joining through Contract. Denormalized for fast aggregation.
★ RECOMMENDED. Room ID this transaction relates to. Enables room-level P&L — the most granular financial view in the system.
